f_night.png at 18:25: queued customer grey square left of grid, eating green on (0,0), cooking orange on (2,0) with lit stove (1,0), seated blue on (3,3); panel Coins 0, Served 0, Lost 0, 18:25, Speed: Fast.
Title, settings, paused, summary and ledger frames show their texts with '> ' on the chosen entry (> Ledger, > Difficulty: Hard, > Title, > Back); summary shows Night over and its numbers.

README gives keys and how to play, says kept things are in the --settings folder (settings.json), and gives both commands; run from scratch exactly as written, they print the state and write frame.png.

defects: Every frame shows a column of 8 small unlabelled buttons at the bottom right: the game's hidden counter buttons (its way of making repeated words count) are drawn on screen.

A headless run with --ticks 0 and a kept folder prints defaults (ledger [], replay_ready false, no Replay on the title), not the kept things; kept values only arrive at the first tick (the README admits this).
The kept folder also holds engine bookkeeping (engine.instances, projects.json) and the c1..c7 press counters in settings.json.
During a replay the state's grid and stock show the replayed night's grid, not the layout grid; the README says so.

trace.how: context, new, read_again and how far the context grew are the run's own records. written_out a request is its growth less its answers (characters / 4), scaled to the run's exact total; of_which_unseen is that less the visible text (thinking). cost is what the request read and wrote, weighted; carried is what reading again what it added cost at every later request (start.carried: the same for what every request starts from). reading + writing is in_the_ledger
